subtitle: PCSX2
_subtitle_source: subtitle names the backend the player will actually run, the same way 18 manifests say "BizHawk".
_platform_source: the world's own README: "an Archipelago randomizer implementation for the PlayStation 2 game Road Trip Adventure". Its setup guide requires "[PCSX2] v2.0 or higher".
_drafted_note: Drafted 2026-08-25 from the world's OWN repository -- its __init__.py, archipelago.json, setup guide and README, read that day. No field is filled in from memory or from what other games on the same console do.
_ap_world_name_source: the world's own archipelago.json: {"game": "Road Trip Adventure"}, agreeing with the World class in __init__.py.
description: Road Trip Adventure as a multiworld. Parts, collectibles, overworld items and licences are shuffled, and each town must be unlocked from the item pool. Requires the player's own NTSC-U disc and PCSX2 v2.0 or newer with PINE enabled on slot 28011.
_description_source: written by us from the world's own structure and its setup guide's stated requirements. No text is copied from the game.
_checks_verified_note: FALSE. Nobody has played this. For a kind=world game the checks travel through the WORLD'S client, not through London -- so what is unproven here is not a RAM map of ours (there is none) but the whole chain: apworld installs, emulator starts over the bridge, the world's client attaches and carries a check. London warns at launch while this is false, which is exactly right until a tester reports one.
_requires_source: PS2 title. The setup guide lists the disc among the player's own requirements: "Road Trip NTSC disc image".

rom.description: Your own Road Trip Adventure disc image for PlayStation 2 -- the NTSC-U release
rom._description_source: the setup guide: "Road Trip NTSC disc image". The randomizer page adds "Currently, only the NTSC-U release is supported."
rom._hash_note: ⭐ The one game of these eight that states a checksum. The setup guide gives it outright: "MD5 checksum: e1598a1a2b1a296dbeae90927172d52a". Copied from the author's own words, not computed here -- so London can actually reject a wrong file for this game instead of only warning.

emulator.name: PCSX2
emulator._source: the setup guide, word for word: "[PCSX2] v2.0 or higher". Stated as a floor, so recorded as a minimum.

client.name: Road Trip Client
client._name_source: the world registers it under this exact name in its __init__.py, and its setup guide says "run the Road Trip client" and "If the Road Trip client is missing from the list, you likely do not have the .apworld file in the custom_worlds folder."
client._kind_source: the world ships and registers its OWN Archipelago client: its __init__.py does `components.append(Component("Road Trip Client", ..., component_type=Type.CLIENT))`, and the transport is the world's own -- client/pine/, with PCSX2 and PINE named throughout client/__init__.py. The setup guide is explicit that the CLIENT patches the game: "The game is patched entirely in memory by the client, and does not modify your ROM at all." London must NOT read memory for this game.
client._protocol_source: extensions/pcsx2/extension.json declares {"protocol": "pine"}, Systems ["PS2"]. The world speaks PINE itself (client/pine/), and the setup guide has the player enable PINE in PCSX2 on slot 28011.
client._lua_note: No Lua. PINE is spoken to PCSX2 directly.

apworld._source: the author's own releases page; the newest release read 25 Aug 2026 is v0.2.0, carrying roadtrip.apworld and a sample YAML.
apworld._world_version_source: the world's archipelago.json: {"world_version": "0.2.0"}, matching the newest release tag.
apworld._minimum_ap_version_source: the world's archipelago.json: {"minimum_ap_version": "0.6.6"}. Our client is 0.6.7, so this is satisfied.

_patch_extension_source: read from the world's own source, 25 Aug 2026: the 8 .py files at the top of the repository were searched. No APPatchExtension, no APProcedurePatch, no patch_file_ending. The setup guide says the same thing in the author's own words: "Does this game have a patch file? Nope!"
_patch_note: There is deliberately NO `patch` block, and here the world says so itself: "The game is patched entirely in memory by the client, and does not modify your ROM at all."

world_by.name: Phenra
world_by._authors_source: the world names them itself: archipelago.json {"authors": ["Phenra"]}.
world_by._source: the repository the world is published from; its own source, archipelago.json and setup guide are what this manifest was written against.
world_by._licence_source: the GitHub API reports spdx_id MIT for the repository, which carries a LICENSE.txt (25 Aug 2026).

credits._game_by_note: Not recorded rather than guessed. The game is the property of its publisher and is never distributed here; the player supplies their own copy. The Archipelago world is its authors' work. Only the plugin itself is by solida1987.
